content.what_it_is: Python (numpy/matplotlib) snapshot-plot script placed in the vessel_types_compare case but byte-identical to vessel_flat_bottom/postprocessing/plot_wave_vessel.py (same SHA-256): its header comment says 'Plot Flat Vessel Waves' (L1) and its data path still points at the vessel_flat_bottom case. It resolves fdir = $HOME/FUNWAVE-TVD/simple_cases/vessel_flat_bottom/work/output (L11-L12), loads eta_00001 for grid sizing (L13-L14, L17), builds x,y with dx=dy=1.0 (L18-L22), selects snapshots nfile=[20, 40] with labels sec=['20','40'] (L24-L25), creates an 8x5-inch, 200-dpi figure (L28-L32), and per snapshot (L34-L51): loads eta_<fnum> (L35-L37), pcolor with coolwarm in stacked subplots (L39-L41), title 'Time = <sec> sec', tight axes, Y/X labels, eta (m) colorbar, clim(-1.5, 1.5) (L43-L51). Saves eta_flat_vessel.png (L53).
entities: script (no function/class definitions; top-level Python script)
HOME — user home directory from environment (L11)
fdir — run output directory pointing at vessel_flat_bottom (L12)
eta — surface elevation, sizing load then per snapshot (L14, L37)

equations.expr: x = np.asarray([float(xa)*dx for xa in range(m)])

io.name: stacked pcolor panels of eta at 20 s and 40 s with colorbars

unresolved: The file is an unmodified copy of the vessel_flat_bottom script: it reads from the vessel_flat_bottom output path (L12) and saves eta_flat_vessel.png (L53), so run as-is in vessel_types_compare it does not plot this case's own output; also its snapshots [20,40] and clim [-1.5,1.5] differ from the MATLAB sibling in this directory ([5,10], [-2.5,2.5]).
os.environ['HOME'] (L11) fails on Windows despite the L10 comment addressing Windows users.
Snapshot labels assume a 1 s output interval; unverifiable here.
